newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Sidek gains on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Sidek gains on speculation.

text.p: Shares of Mexican conglomerate Grupo Sidek were sharply higher in late trade Wednesday on speculation ahead of an expected plan to restructure the troubled firm's finances, dealers said.
Sidek's A shares were up 9.29 percent while its benchmark B series was also up 4.71 percent.
Dealers said brokerage Accival, of the financial group Banamex-Accival, was doing most of the buying. Banamex bank is one of Sidek's main creditors.
"If Accival is putting money into Sidek, maybe they are expecting some sort of news soon," a dealer said.
Sidek's director general Luis Rebollar recently told reporters the group expects to announce a final restructuring plan before November.

The 1994 peso devaluation left Sidek with unpayable dollar debt. The company halted debt payments last year and has since been in ongoing talks with creditors to restructure about $2.1 billion in debt.
